the implementation of a graded RTW program in the German statutory health insurance system leads to a reduction of sickness benefits and sickness absence, but does not reduce medical costs in the follow-up period.
the implementation of a graded RTW program in Germany is associated with slightly increased expenditures on ambulatory services and on pharmaceuticals but with reduced expenditures on hospital care.
RTW participation leads to a reduction of sickness benefits and a slightly higher medical expenditure in a follow-up of 540 days.

the question of whether the RTW participation is associated with a higher demand of medical services in the follow-up period.
the long-term effects of RTW programs and their impact on medical costs and medical demand.
